transcription.tex: \textbf{Force diagrams}\par Weight \(W=mg\) acts vertically downwards. Normal reaction \(R\) is perpendicular to the contact surface. Tension acts along a taut string, away from the body. Friction opposes relative sliding or its tendency.\par \textbf{Newton’s first law}\par Zero resultant force means constant velocity (including rest).\par An object has forces 30 N right, 30 N left, 40 N up and 5 N down. Find the resultant.
\[F_x=30-30=0,\qquad F_y=40-5=35.\] The resultant is 35 N upwards. Acceleration is in the direction of the resultant force.

transcription.tex: 1. Forces act on a particle: \(P\) N right, 3 N left, 5 N up and 5 N down. Find the resultant.\par 2. Forces act on another particle: 5 N right, 7 N left, 4 N up and 6 N down. Find the resultant and its magnitude.

2. \(\mathbf F=-2\mathbf i-2\mathbf j\) N.\[|\mathbf F|=\sqrt{8}=2\sqrt2\text{ N}.\] It points diagonally down and left.

transcription.tex: A force \({F}_{1}\) acts in the direction of \(i\) and a force \({F}_{2}\) acts at an angle of \(\theta \) to \(i\), as shown.\par Show that the resultant force has magnitude \(\sqrt{{F}_{1}^{2}+{F}_{2}^{2}+2{F}_{1}{F}_{2}\cos \theta }\)
\[\mathbf R=(F_1+F_2\cos\theta)\mathbf i+F_2\sin\theta\mathbf j\] \[|\mathbf R|^2=(F_1+F_2\cos\theta)^2+F_2^2\sin^2\theta\]
\[=F_1^2+2F_1F_2\cos\theta+F_2^2(\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta)\] \[=F_1^2+F_2^2+2F_1F_2\cos\theta.\] Take the non-negative square root.

transcription.tex: 11. The engine of a van of mass 400 kg cuts out when it is moving along a straight horizontal road with speed 16 \(\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). The van comes to rest without the brakes being applied. In a model of the situation it is assumed that the van is subject to a resistive force which has constant magnitude of 200 N. \par (a) Find how long it takes the van to stop. \par (b) Find how far the van travels before it stops. \par (c) Comment on the suitability of the modelling assumption.

transcription.tex: Particles \(P,Q\), masses 5 kg and 3 kg, are joined by a light inextensible string on a rough horizontal plane. A horizontal 40 N force pulls \(P\) away from \(Q\). Friction is 10 N on \(P\) and 6 N on \(Q\).\par a. Find their acceleration.

Alternatively, for the separate particles:\[40-T-10=5a,\qquad T-6=3a.\] Adding gives \(24=8a\), as before.

transcription.tex: \textbf{Newton’s third law}\par Interaction forces on two different bodies are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.\par [Textbook] A light scale-pan is attached to a vertical light inextensible string. The scale-pan carries two masses \(A\) and \(B\). The mass of \(A\) is 400g and the mass of \(B\) is 600g. \(A\) rests on top of \(B\), as shown in the diagram.\par The scale-pan is raised vertically, using the string, with acceleration 0.5 \(\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). \par (a) Find the tension in the string.\par (b) Find the force exerted on mass \(B\) by mass \(A\).\par (c) Find the force exerted on mass \(B\) by the scale-pan.
a. \(T-1g=1(0.5)\Rightarrow T=10.3\) N.
b. For \(A\): \(R-0.4g=0.4(0.5)\Rightarrow R=4.12\) N. Hence \(A\) exerts 4.12 N downwards on \(B\).
c. For both masses: \(N-1g=1(0.5)\Rightarrow N=10.3\) N upwards.

The engine of the car produces a constant horizontal driving force on the car of magnitude 1200 N. \par (a) Show that the acceleration of the car and trailer is \(0.75\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). transcription.tex: [Textbook] Particles \(P\) and \(Q\), of masses \(2m\) and \(3m\), are attached to the ends of a light inextensible string. The string passes over a small smooth fixed pulley and the masses hang with the string taut. The system is released from rest.\par (a) Write down an equation of motion for \(P\) and for \(Q\).\par (b) Find the acceleration of each mass.\par (c) Find the tension in the string.\par (d) Find the force exerted on the pulley by the string.\par (e) Find the distance moved by \(Q\) in the first 4 s, assuming that \(P\) does not reach the pulley.
For \(P\) upwards and \(Q\) downwards:\[T-2mg=2ma,\quad3mg-T=3ma.\] \[a=g/5,\quad T=12mg/5.\]
Both string forces on the pulley act downwards:\[F=2T=24mg/5.\] \[s=\tfrac12(g/5)(4^2)=15.7\text{ m}.\]
A light string over a smooth pulley has equal tension on both sides. The taut inextensible string gives equal acceleration magnitudes in this fixed-pulley arrangement.

transcription.tex: Two particles \(A\) and \(B\) have masses \(5m\) and \(km\) respectively, where \(k<5\). The system is held at rest with the string taut, the hanging parts of the string vertical and with \(A\) and \(B\) at the same height above a horizontal plane, as shown in Figure 4. transcription.tex: 1. Two particles A and B of masses 4 kg and 3 kg respectively are connected by a light inextensible string which passes over a small smooth fixed pulley. The particles are released from rest with the string taut. \par (a) Find the tension in the string. When A has travelled a distance of 2 m it strikes the ground and immediately comes to rest. \par (b) Find the speed of A when it hits the ground. \par (c) Assuming that B does not hit the pulley, find the greatest height that B reaches above its initial position.
\[4g-T=4a,\quad T-3g=3a\Rightarrow a=g/7.\] \[T=24g/7=33.6\text{ N}.\]
Additional free rise \(=v^2/(2g)=2/7\) m.\par Total rise \(=2+2/7=16/7\) m.

transcription.tex: \textbf{2.} Two particles \(P\) and \(Q\) have masses \(km\) and \(3m\) respectively, where \(k<3\). The particles are connected by a light inextensible string which passes over a smooth light fixed pulley. The system is held at rest with the string taut, the hanging parts of the string vertical and with \(P\) and \(Q\) at the same height above a horizontal plane, as shown in the diagram. The system is released from rest. After release, \(Q\) descends with acceleration \(\tfrac13g\).\par (a) Calculate the tension in the string as \(Q\) descends. (3 marks)\par (b) Show that \(k=1.5\). (3 marks)\par (c) State how you have used the information that the pulley is smooth. (1 mark)\par After descending for 1.8 s, the particle \(Q\) reaches the plane. It is immediately brought to rest by the impact with the plane. The initial distance between \(P\) and the pulley is such that, in the subsequent motion, \(P\) does not reach the pulley.\par (d) Show that the greatest height, in metres, reached by \(P\) above the plane is \(1.26g\). (7 marks)
\[3mg-T=3m(g/3)\Rightarrow T=2mg.\] \[T-kmg=km(g/3)\Rightarrow k=1.5.\] Smooth pulley gives equal tensions.
Initial height \(h=\tfrac12(g/3)(1.8^2)=0.54g\).\par Speed at landing \(v=0.6g\). Extra rise \(=v^2/(2g)=0.18g\).\[H=2(0.54g)+0.18g=1.26g\text{ m}.\]

transcription.tex: 3. Two particles A and B have masses m kg and 3 kg respectively, where m > 3. The particles are connected by a light inextensible string which passes over a smooth, fixed pulley. Initially A is 2.5 m above horizontal ground. The particles are released from rest with the string taut and the hanging parts of the string vertical, as shown in the figure. After A has been descending for 1.25 s, it strikes the ground. Particle A reaches the ground before B has reached the pulley. \par (a) Show that the acceleration of B as it ascends is \(3.2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). (3 marks) \par (b) Find the tension in the string as A descends. (3 marks) \par (c) Show that \(m=65/11\) (4 marks)
a. \(2.5=\tfrac12a(1.25^2)\Rightarrow a=3.2\text{ m/s}^2\).
b. \(T-3g=3(3.2)\Rightarrow T=39\) N.
c. \(mg-T=ma\Rightarrow m=39/(9.8-3.2)=65/11\) kg.

transcription.tex: 3. (continued) The particles were released from rest with the string taut and the hanging parts of the string vertical. After A has been descending for 1.25 s, it strikes the ground. \par (d) State  how you have used the information that the string is inextensible. (1 mark) When A strikes the ground it does not rebound and the string becomes slack. Particle B then moves freely under gravity, without reaching the pulley, until the string becomes taut again. \par (e) Find the time between the instant when A strikes the ground and the instant when the string becomes taut again. (6 marks)
d. While taut, the fixed string length makes the particles’ acceleration magnitudes equal. Equal tension instead follows from the light string and smooth pulley.
e. At impact, \(u_B=3.2(1.25)=4\) m/s. The string becomes taut when \(B\) returns to this height:\[0=4t-4.9t^2\Rightarrow t=\frac{40}{49}=0.816\text{ s}.\]

transcription.tex: 5. A box P of mass 2.5 kg rests on a rough horizontal table and is attached to one end of a light inextensible string. The string passes over a small smooth pulley fixed at the edge of the table. The other end of the string is attached to a sphere Q of mass 1.5 kg which hangs freely below the pulley. The magnitude of the frictional force between P and the table is k N. The system is released from rest with the string taut. After release, Q descends a distance of 0.8 m in 0.75 s. \par (a) Modelling P and Q as particles: (i) calculate the acceleration of Q (ii) show that the tension in the string is 10.4 N (to 3 s.f.) (iii) find the value of k. \par (b) State how in your calculations you have used the information that the string is inextensible.
\[k=T-2.5a=3.3222\ldots=3.32\text{ N}.\] Retain unrounded values during the calculation.
While the string is taut, its fixed length gives equal acceleration magnitudes for the box and sphere.
